description: I am interested in Data Analysis and animation and looking forward to combine both to make an interactive fun game.
summary:
TerraQuest Beats: The Earth Information Jukebox is an interactive 3D web application that transforms NASA climate visualizations, satellite drought maps, and natural hazard charts into real-time music.
To solve the "Earth Information Jukebox" challenge, we built a browser-native sonification engine using the HTML5 Canvas API and Web Audio API. As a glowing scanline sweeps across real-world visualizations—spanning global temperature anomalies, shrinking glaciers, droughts, wildfires, volcanoes, and earthquakes across 15+ global hotspots—our algorithm reads pixel heights and color intensities in real time and maps them onto a harmonious C-major pentatonic scale.
By turning sight into sound, TerraQuest Beats makes complex Earth science accessible to blind and low-vision learners while helping everyone hear subtle climate patterns and sudden environmental shifts. Each location on our 3D globe combines scientific briefings from our guide, Terra-Bot, an interactive "Test Your Ears" audio quiz, and full keyboard and screen-reader navigation.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

TerraQuest Beats: The Earth Information Jukebox is a browser-based, interactive 3D planetary jukebox that translates Earth science visualizations into real-time music. Users explore a 3D Earth dotted with 15+ real-world climate and hazard hotspots—covering global warming, glacial retreat, droughts, wildfires, cyclones, volcanic eruptions, and earthquakes.

Selecting any location opens a 3-tab learning experience guided by our animated mascot, Terra-Bot:

  1. Space Mission: Provides scientific context and safety guidance for the dataset.
  2. Game & Quiz ("Test Your Ears"): Challenges users to identify environmental trends purely by listening to the audio.
  3. Earth Jukebox: Renders the scientific chart or satellite map onto an HTML5 <canvas> and sweeps an animated scanline across it. Using getImageData() pixel inspection and the browser’s built-in Web Audio API, our engine reads vertical line heights and color intensities in real time across three smart scanning modes (Full Time-Series Chart, Split-Panel Chart, and Satellite Map-Color Mode) and maps them onto a C-major pentatonic scale (C D E G A).

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Accessibility First: By pairing auditory sonification with full keyboard navigation (Arrow keys, Enter, Spacebar) and ARIA screen-reader announcements, blind and low-vision learners can independently explore complex NASA Earth data.
  • Intuitive Science Communication: Hearing a melody drop as glacier thickness shrinks or surge during a heatwave creates an immediate emotional and intuitive connection to climate change for students and the public.

Tools, Languages & Software Used

  • Languages & Web APIs: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (ES6+), Web Audio API (real-time oscillators and gain control), and HTML5 Canvas API (pixel-to-pitch computer vision).
  • 3D Graphics & Hosting: Three.js for the interactive 3D Earth globe, Photopea and EZGIF for frame extraction and image preparation, Canva for presentation visuals, and GitHub Pages for live web hosting.
  • AI Assistance: Claude and ChatGPT were used to assist with JavaScript architecture, Web Audio synthesis logic, and accessibility refinements.

Creativity & Design Factors Considered

Raw pixel-to-frequency conversion often produces harsh, fatiguing noise. Our team prioritized musicality alongside scientific accuracy by quantizing data values to a harmonious pentatonic scale, adding a transparent "How It Sounds" legend on every chart, and engineering specialized scan zones so multi-panel graphs and satellite maps translate cleanly into meaningful soundscapes.
